reason: Both correctly identify water-cooled condenser drying as normal, but Conversation 1 does so with accurate information: a realistic 10-60 litre per cycle figure, a sensible pence-per-cycle cost that directly answers the homeowner's water-meter worry, well-bounded leak checks (puddles, water running when idle, wet clothes), and a request for make/model. Conversation 2 understates water use at '1-2 litres per load', wrongly says condenser tumble dryers use water cooling, and then pushes an unnecessary 'turn the tap off mid-cycle' test, reassuring the homeowner it is 'perfectly safe' and the machine will just 'cool down slightly slower' when in fact removing condenser water defeats the drying process and may trigger a fault. Conversation 2's interactive confirmation of a dry floor and pump noise is a plus, but its inaccurate figures and an ill-founded test on a machine that has no fault outweigh that; Conversation 1 reaches the right conclusion more honestly and without inventing checks.
